question: Who among the following is an award-winning folk dancer from Arunachal Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sang Jangmu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sang Jangmu is recognised as an award-winning folk dancer from Arunachal Pradesh, honoured for her long-standing contribution to preserving and performing the state's traditional tribal folk-dance heritage. (लोक नृत्यकार — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

 

• Arunachal Pradesh has a rich diversity of tribal folk dances performed by communities such as the Nyishi, Adi, Apatani, Monpa and Wancho, and national cultural awards periodically recognise grassroots artistes who keep these traditions alive.

 

• Such recognitions are usually for decades of community-level effort in teaching, choreographing and performing traditional dance forms, often without formal institutional backing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The North-East region as a whole has seen a steady rise in national cultural honours for folk artistes, reflecting the government's continued focus on recognising indigenous and tribal art forms.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh's folk dances are typically linked to agricultural festivals, community rituals and warrior traditions of its many tribes.

 

NOTE

 

• Meena Nayak (Option 2): Not the folk dancer associated with this Arunachal Pradesh award context.

 

• Tarubala Debbarma (Option 3): A name associated with tribal culture of the North-East, but not the correct match here.

 

• Balkar Siddhu (Option 4): Not linked to Arunachal Pradesh's folk-dance award in this context.

question: By whose hand was the original Constitution of India written (hand-calligraphed) in English?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prem Bihari Narayan Raizada.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The original English text of the Constitution of India was hand-calligraphed in a flowing italic style by Prem Bihari Narayan Raizada, a renowned calligrapher of Delhi. (मूल संविधान की सुलेखन — प्रेम बिहारी नारायण रायज़ादा)

 

• Raizada used around 300 different pen-nibs and took nearly six months, without any payment — his only request was that his name, and his grandfather's name, appear on every page of the Constitution, which was granted.

 

• The Constitution's pages were also profusely illustrated by artists of Shantiniketan under the guidance of Nandalal Bose, depicting scenes from Indian civilisational history.

 

• The Hindi version of the Constitution was separately hand-calligraphed by Vasant Krishna Vaidya.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day / Samvidhan Divas), and it came into force on 26 January 1950.

 

• The original handwritten copies (English and Hindi) are preserved in special helium-filled cases in the Library of the Parliament of India.

 

NOTE

 

• S.N. Mukherjee (Option 1): He was the Chief Draftsman of the Constituent Assembly, responsible for the final wording/drafting of the Constitution, not its calligraphy.

 

• H.V.R. Iyengar (Option 3): An ICS officer who served the Constituent Assembly in an administrative capacity and later became RBI Governor; not the calligrapher.

 

• Vasant Krishna Vaidya (Option 4): He calligraphed the Hindi version, not the English version, of the Constitution.

question: The Central Government has approved the Print and Digital Media Association (PADMA) as a self-regulatory body for publishers of news and current affairs across the country. Who heads this organisation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mulchand Garg.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Print and Digital Media Association (PADMA) was approved by the Central Government (Ministry of Information and Broadcasting) in December 2022 as a self-regulatory body for print and digital news publishers. (स्व-नियामक संस्था — मूलचंद गर्ग)

 

• PADMA is headed by Mool Chand Garg, a former Judge of the Delhi High Court, who serves as its Chairperson.

 

• The body was recognised under the Press and Registration of Periodicals (PRP) Act, 2023 / erstwhile PRB Act framework as an appellate mechanism for grievances against digital news publishers, alongside the Press Council of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• PADMA's recognition came in the backdrop of the IT Rules, 2021 (amended), which brought digital news publishers under a structured grievance-redressal system.

 

• Other members of PADMA's governing body include senior figures drawn from journalism and public broadcasting.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahesh Kumar Sharma (Option 1): Not the head of PADMA.

 

• Krishnendra Pratap Singh (Option 2): Not the head of PADMA.

 

• Girdhar Aramane (Option 4): A senior IAS officer known for holding government secretary-level posts, but not the head of PADMA.

question: The 2004 Padma Bhushan awardee and classical dancer Alarmel Valli is known for which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alarmel Valli is one of India's foremost exponents of Bharatanatyam, trained in the Pandanallur (Kalakshetra-adjacent) style under Guru Chokkalingam Pillai. (भरतनाट्यम — अलर्मेल वल्ली)

 

• She was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2004, having earlier received the Padma Shri in 1991, for her contribution to classical dance.

 

• She is known for her lyrical, expressive style (abhinaya) and has performed and choreographed extensively on Bharatanatyam repertoire including Tamil devotional poetry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu and is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, traditionally performed in temples.

 

• Other renowned Bharatanatyam exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Padma Subrahmanyam.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 2): A classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, not associated with Alarmel Valli.

 

• Chhau (Option 3): A semi-classical martial dance form from Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal.

 

• Odissi (Option 4): A classical dance form of Odisha; notable exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra and Sonal Mansingh.

question: Who among the following was the Chief Draftsman of the Constituent Assembly, responsible for preparing the draft of the Constitution document?
solution_text:
The correct answer is S.N. Mukherjee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• S.N. Mukherjee (Sir Benegal Narsing Rau's associate) served as the Chief Draftsman of the Constituent Assembly, responsible for finalising the wording and structure of the Constitution's draft. (मुख्य प्रारूपकार — एस.एन. मुखर्जी)

 

• Mukherjee was praised, including by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, for his ability to convey complex constitutional ideas in the simplest possible language and to arrange provisions in a systematic, cross-referenced form.

 

• The overall constitutional advisor to the Assembly was Sir Benegal Narsing Rau, who prepared the original draft before it went to the Drafting Committee headed by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly was constituted on 29 August 1947 with Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as its Chairman.

 

• The Constitution was hand-calligraphed by Prem Bihari Narayan Raizada (English) and Vasant Krishna Vaidya (Hindi).

 

NOTE

 

• H.V.R. Iyengar (Option 1): An ICS officer associated with the Constituent Assembly's secretariat, later RBI Governor; not the Chief Draftsman.

 

• Vasant Krishna Vaidya (Option 2): Calligraphed the Hindi version of the Constitution; not the Chief Draftsman.

 

• K.M. Munshi (Option 3): A prominent member of the Drafting Committee and the Constituent Assembly, not its Chief Draftsman.

question: Identify the odd one out from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Construction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian economic activities are broadly classified into three sectors — Primary, Secondary and Tertiary (Services). (निर्माण क्षेत्र — द्वितीयक क्षेत्र)

 

• Transport and Communication, Banking and Insurance, and Hotels and Restaurants are all part of the Tertiary (Services) Sector, as they provide services rather than producing physical goods.

 

• Construction, on the other hand, belongs to the Secondary (Industrial) Sector, since it involves converting raw materials (cement, steel, bricks, etc.) into a finished physical structure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Primary sector includes agriculture, forestry, fishing and mining — activities directly using natural resources.

 

• The Secondary sector also includes manufacturing and electricity/gas/water supply along with construction.

 

NOTE

 

• Transport and Communication (Option 1): A tertiary/service-sector activity, unlike Construction.

 

• Banking and Insurance (Option 2): A tertiary/service-sector activity, unlike Construction.

 

• Hotels and Restaurants (Option 4): A tertiary/service-sector activity, unlike Construction.

question: Which one of the following is NOT among the industry categories classified under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956?
option_1: Industries where the public sector takes the lead, and the private sector plays a supplementary role
option_2: Industries exclusively owned by the State
solution_text:
The correct answer is Industries in the cooperative sector.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR), 1956 classified industries into three categories (Schedules A, B and C) based on the role of the State. (औद्योगिक नीति संकल्प 1956 — तीन श्रेणियाँ)

 

• Schedule A: Industries whose future development was the exclusive responsibility of the State (e.g., defence, atomic energy, railways).

 

• Schedule B: Industries in which the State would increasingly establish new undertakings, but private enterprise would also supplement the State's effort.

 

• Schedule C: All remaining industries left to the private sector, though subject to the general economic and social policy of the State.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The IPR, 1956 is often called the 'Economic Constitution of India' or the second major statement of India's industrial policy after the IPR of 1948.

 

• It emphasised the mixed economy model, giving the State a commanding role in core and strategic industries.

 

NOTE

 

• Industries where the public sector leads and private sector supplements (Option 1): This matches Schedule B of the IPR 1956.

 

• Industries exclusively owned by the State (Option 2): This matches Schedule A of the IPR 1956.

 

• Industries in the private sector (Option 3): This matches Schedule C of the IPR 1956.

question: Which one of the following is NOT among the reasons for the obstacles faced by the poor in accessing credit schemes?
option_2: Lack of collateral or credit history along with a clear title showing legal ownership
option_3: Lenders prefer to deal in a small number of large-value loans in order to reduce administrative costs
option_4: Lack of a stable source of income
solution_text:
The correct answer is Poor information about administrative (monitoring) costs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The poor face several well-documented obstacles in accessing formal credit, discussed in the context of financial inclusion. (गरीबों की ऋण तक पहुँच — बाधाएँ)

 

• A major barrier is the lack of collateral (land, property with a clear legal title) or a documented credit history, which formal lenders require before sanctioning a loan.

 

• Formal lenders also prefer to minimise administrative/monitoring costs by disbursing a small number of large loans rather than a large number of small loans to the poor, making it harder for the poor to be served.

 

• An irregular or unstable income further makes the poor a riskier and less attractive category of borrower for formal lending institutions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Because of these obstacles, the poor are pushed toward informal sources of credit (moneylenders, traders, employers), which often charge very high interest rates and can trap borrowers in debt.

 

• Institutions like SHGs (Self-Help Groups), cooperatives and microfinance institutions were promoted precisely to overcome these access barriers for the poor.

 

NOTE

 

• Lack of collateral/clear title (Option 2): A genuine, well-documented reason poor borrowers are excluded from formal credit.

 

• Lenders preferring large-value loans (Option 3): A genuine reason, since formal lenders find small loans to the poor administratively costlier per rupee lent.

 

• Lack of stable income (Option 4): A genuine reason, as irregular income raises perceived credit risk for lenders.

question: Which of the following Indian players won a title in Men's Doubles at the Bangkok Open (Tennis) 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yuki Bhambri - Saketh Myneni.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian pair of Yuki Bhambri and Saketh Myneni won the Men's Doubles title at the Bangkok Open Challenger, 2023. (पुरुष युगल खिताब — यूकी भांबरी-साकेत मायनेनी)

 

• Both players are established doubles specialists on the ATP/Challenger circuit and have partnered successfully on multiple occasions.

 

• Bangkok Open is part of the ATP Challenger Tour, providing ranking points and prize money below the main ATP Tour level.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Yuki Bhambri has also had success in Grand Slam mixed doubles and men's doubles events over his career.

 

• Saketh Myneni is a veteran Indian doubles player who has represented India in the Davis Cup.

 

NOTE

 

• Yuki Bhambri - Purav Raja (Option 1): Incorrect pairing for this event.

 

• Divij Sharan - Yuki Bhambri (Option 2): Incorrect pairing for this event.

 

• Sumit Nagal - Saketh Myneni (Option 4): Incorrect pairing for this event.

question: ________ are the amphibians of the plant kingdom.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bryophyta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bryophytes are called the 'Amphibians of the Plant Kingdom' because, like amphibian animals, they can live in soil but are dependent on external/free water for sexual reproduction (fertilisation requires water for the motile male gametes to swim to the egg). (उभयचर पादप — ब्रायोफाइटा)

 

• Bryophytes include mosses and liverworts; they lack true vascular tissue (xylem/phloem) and true roots, stems or leaves.

 

• They are typically found in cool, damp, shady places and represent one of the earliest lineages of land plants.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common examples of Bryophyta are Funaria (moss) and Marchantia (liverwort).

 

• Plant classification (by Whittaker/botanical taxonomy) commonly groups plants as Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms in order of increasing complexity.

 

NOTE

 

• Thallophyta (Option 1): Includes algae and fungi-like plant groups with an undifferentiated body (thallus); not the 'amphibians of plant kingdom'.

 

• Gymnosperms (Option 2): Seed-bearing plants with 'naked seeds' (e.g., pine, cycas); fully adapted to land, not amphibious in this sense.

 

• Pteridophyta (Option 4): Vascular plants like ferns that also need water for fertilisation but already possess vascular tissue, unlike bryophytes; they are not the group traditionally termed 'amphibians of the plant kingdom'.

question: Which of the following states is the largest producer of lignite coal in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tamil Nadu is the largest producer of lignite (brown coal) in India, with the major reserves and mining/power operations concentrated at Neyveli in Cuddalore district. (लिग्नाइट कोयला — तमिलनाडु)

 

• Lignite is a low-grade, soft, brownish coal with lower carbon content and calorific value compared to bituminous coal, but it is an important fuel for thermal power generation in Tamil Nadu.

 

• Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC India Limited) is the major public-sector undertaking engaged in lignite mining and power generation in the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other states with notable lignite reserves include Rajasthan (Barmer, Bikaner) and Gujarat (Kutch), but their production is much smaller than Tamil Nadu's.

 

• India's largest coal (bituminous, not lignite) reserves and production, by contrast, are concentrated in Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand (Option 1): A leading producer of bituminous coal, not the top lignite producer.

 

• Gujarat (Option 3): Has lignite deposits (e.g., Kutch) but produces far less than Tamil Nadu.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Not a major lignite-producing state.

question: Who among the following won the Maharashtra Bhushan Award for the year 2020 in Indian Music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asha Bhosle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Veteran playback singer Asha Bhosle was conferred the Maharashtra Bhushan Award for the year 2020 (the award ceremony was held in 2021) in recognition of her lifetime contribution to Indian music. (महाराष्ट्र भूषण पुरस्कार — आशा भोंसले)

 

• The Maharashtra Bhushan Award is the highest civilian award conferred by the Government of Maharashtra, instituted in 1996.

 

• Asha Bhosle has sung in numerous languages across decades and holds a Guinness World Record for the most studio recordings by any singer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Asha Bhosle is the younger sister of legendary singer Lata Mangeshkar, who herself received several of India's highest civilian honours including the Bharat Ratna.

 

• Other Maharashtra Bhushan awardees across different years span fields such as literature, sports, social work, and science.

 

NOTE

 

• Shreya Ghoshal (Option 1): A prominent playback singer, but not the 2020 Maharashtra Bhushan awardee.

 

• Alka Yagnik (Option 2): A celebrated playback singer, but not the 2020 Maharashtra Bhushan awardee.

 

• Sunidhi Chauhan (Option 3): A well-known playback singer, but not the 2020 Maharashtra Bhushan awardee.

question: In which year did Carl Anderson discover a positively charged particle known as the 'positron', whose mass appears to be equal to that of an electron?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1932.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• American physicist Carl David Anderson discovered the positron (the antiparticle of the electron) in 1932, while studying cosmic ray tracks in a cloud chamber. (पॉज़िट्रॉन की खोज — कार्ल एंडरसन, 1932)

 

• The positron carries a positive electric charge but has the same mass as an electron, making it the electron's antimatter counterpart.

 

• This discovery provided the first experimental evidence of antimatter, confirming a prediction made earlier by physicist Paul Dirac.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Carl Anderson was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1936 for the discovery of the positron.

 

• The positron's discovery laid the foundation for later developments in particle physics, including PET (Positron Emission Tomography) scanning technology used in medicine.

 

NOTE

 

• 1942 (Option 1): Not the year of the positron's discovery.

 

• 1922 (Option 2): Not the year of the positron's discovery.

 

• 1912 (Option 3): Not the year of the positron's discovery; this period is more associated with early cosmic ray research by Victor Hess.

question: Since absolute equality is impossible, Article ________ of the Indian Constitution provides that the right to equality, as well as the equal protection of laws, is subject to reasonable classification.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 14.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 14 of the Indian Constitution guarantees 'Equality before law and equal protection of laws' to all persons within the territory of India. (समानता का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 14)

 

• Since absolute, mechanical equality among unequal individuals/situations is not practical or just, Article 14 permits 'reasonable classification', provided the classification is based on an intelligible differentia and has a rational nexus with the object sought to be achieved by the law.

 

• This doctrine of reasonable classification has been developed and reaffirmed by the Supreme Court in numerous landmark judgments interpreting Article 14.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 14 is part of the 'Right to Equality' (Articles 14-18) under Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution.

 

• Article 14 applies to both citizens and non-citizens (a 'person'), unlike some other Fundamental Rights restricted only to citizens.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 15 (Option 2): Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.

 

• Article 16 (Option 3): Provides equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.

 

• Article 13 (Option 4): Declares laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights to be void.

question: In 2022, how many individuals received the Arjuna Award for their outstanding performance in sports and games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 25.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 2022, a total of 25 individuals were conferred the Arjuna Award for outstanding performance in sports and games, as part of the National Sports Awards. (अर्जुन पुरस्कार — 25 व्यक्ति, 2022)

 

• The Arjuna Award is instituted by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, to recognise consistent outstanding performance over a period of four years.

 

• The 2022 National Sports Awards ceremony (held at Rashtrapati Bhavan) also conferred the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award and Dronacharya Awards, among others, alongside the Arjuna Awards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Khel Ratna Award is India's highest sporting honour, while the Arjuna Award recognises excellence at the individual sportsperson level.

 

• The Dronacharya Award is conferred on coaches for their contribution to producing medal-winning sportspersons.

 

NOTE

 

• 20 (Option 2): Not the correct count of 2022 Arjuna Award recipients.

 

• 30 (Option 3): Not the correct count of 2022 Arjuna Award recipients.

 

• 31 (Option 4): Not the correct count of 2022 Arjuna Award recipients.

question: Who started the practice of celebrating Nauroz (Nowruz) during the Delhi Sultanate period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghiyasuddin Balban.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ghiyasuddin Balban (r. 1266-1287 CE), a ruler of the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, started the practice of celebrating the Persian festival of Nauroz (Nowruz) at his court. (नौरोज़ उत्सव — गियासुद्दीन बलबन)

 

• Balban introduced elaborate Persian court customs and rigid court etiquette — including *sijda* (prostration) and *paibos* (kissing the ruler's feet) — modelled on Persian Sasanian imperial traditions, to project the Sultan's power, awe and divine right to rule.

 

• The grand Nauroz celebrations, with feasts and gift-giving, were part of Balban's broader strategy to strengthen the prestige and centralised authority of the Sultanate's throne.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Balban is also known for his 'blood and iron' policy, ruthlessly suppressing the nobility (the 'Forty'/Chahalgani) and rebels to consolidate royal power.

 

• He also strengthened the espionage system (barid) and reorganised the military department (Diwan-i-Arz).

 

NOTE

 

• Sikandar Sur (Option 2): A ruler of the Sur dynasty, unrelated to the introduction of Nauroz in the Delhi Sultanate.

 

• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (Option 3): Founder of the Tughlaq dynasty, but not credited with starting the Nauroz tradition.

 

• Shamsuddin Iltutmish (Option 4): An important early Mamluk Sultan known for consolidating the Sultanate and introducing the silver tanka and copper jital, not for starting Nauroz celebrations.

question: According to the 2011 Census of India, which district in India has the lowest literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alirajpur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census of India, Alirajpur district in Madhya Pradesh recorded the lowest literacy rate among all districts of India, at around 37%. (सबसे कम साक्षरता दर — अलीराजपुर, मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• Alirajpur is a predominantly tribal district (largely inhabited by the Bhil and Bhilala communities) carved out of Jhabua district in 2008, and it continues to face challenges in education infrastructure and access.

 

• Districts with low literacy in the 2011 Census were concentrated mainly in tribal-dominated and geographically remote regions of central and eastern India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per the 2011 Census, Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate among Indian states, while among Union Territories, Lakshadweep ranked highest.

 

• India's overall literacy rate as per the 2011 Census was 74.04%.

 

NOTE

 

• Siwan (Option 2): A district of Bihar; not the lowest-literacy district as per the 2011 Census.

 

• Choki (Option 3): Not the lowest-literacy district as per the 2011 Census.

 

• Bemetara (Option 4): A district of Chhattisgarh; not the lowest-literacy district as per the 2011 Census.

question: Under the Indian Constitution's provisions, which Article mentions the right to form cooperative societies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 19(1)(c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 19(1)(c) of the Indian Constitution guarantees citizens the right 'to form associations or unions or co-operative societies'. (सहकारी समितियाँ बनाने का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 19(1)(c))

 

• The words 'or co-operative societies' were specifically inserted into Article 19(1)(c) by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011, which also inserted Article 43-B (Directive Principle promoting cooperative societies) and added Part IX-B to the Constitution.

 

• This right, like other freedoms under Article 19(1), is subject to 'reasonable restrictions' that can be imposed by the State under Article 19(4).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 19(1) guarantees six fundamental freedoms to citizens, including freedom of speech and expression [19(1)(a)] and freedom to assemble peaceably [19(1)(b)].

 

• The Supreme Court in 2021 struck down parts of the 97th Amendment relating to Part IX-B for lack of requisite state ratification, but the amendment to Article 19(1)(c) itself remained unaffected.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 19(1)(a) (Option 1): Freedom of speech and expression, not cooperative societies.

 

• Article 19(1)(b) (Option 3): Freedom to assemble peaceably and without arms, not cooperative societies.

 

• Article 19(1)(d) (Option 4): Freedom to move freely throughout the territory of India, not cooperative societies.

question:
Which of the following is an example of a Capital Receipt?

A) A loan taken from the World Bank to fund a project for saving tigers.

B) Selling a 30% stake in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to private companies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Capital Receipt either creates a liability for the government or reduces its assets. (पूंजीगत प्राप्तियाँ — ऋण और विनिवेश)

 

• Statement A describes a loan/borrowing from the World Bank, which creates a liability (a repayment obligation) for the government — this is a classic capital receipt.

 

• Statement B describes disinvestment (selling government equity/stake in a PSU), which reduces government assets — this is also a capital receipt.

 

• Both borrowings and disinvestment proceeds are recorded under Capital Receipts in the Union Budget, distinct from Revenue Receipts (like tax and non-tax revenue) which neither create a liability nor reduce assets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of Capital Receipts include recovery of loans given by the government and receipts from the sale of government assets.

 

• Revenue Receipts, by contrast, include tax revenue (income tax, GST, etc.) and non-tax revenue (interest, dividends, fees).

 

NOTE

 

• Only A (Option 1): Incorrect, since Statement B is also a valid capital receipt.

 

• Only B (Option 2): Incorrect, since Statement A is also a valid capital receipt.

 

• Neither A nor B (Option 3): Incorrect, since both statements correctly describe capital receipts.

question: In cricket, if the umpire extends both hands horizontally (sideways), it signals a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wide ball.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In cricket, when the umpire extends both arms out horizontally (sideways, parallel to the ground), it signals a 'Wide Ball'. (वाइड बॉल का संकेत — दोनों हाथ फैलाना)

 

• A wide ball is called when the delivery passes too far from the batter for them to be able to play a normal cricketing shot, and it results in an extra run being added to the batting team's total.

 

• Umpire signals are standardised worldwide by the ICC (International Cricket Council) so that scorers and spectators can clearly identify the outcome of each delivery.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A 'No ball' is signalled by the umpire extending one arm horizontally out to the side.

 

• A 'Dead ball' is signalled by crossing and uncrossing the wrists below the waist, while 'Out' is signalled by raising the index finger above the head.

 

NOTE

 

• Dead ball (Option 1): Signalled differently — crossing and uncrossing the wrists below the waist, not extending both arms.

 

• No ball (Option 3): Signalled by extending only one arm horizontally, not both.

 

• Run out (Option 4): Signalled the same way as a normal 'Out' — the umpire raises the index finger overhead.

question: The Pola festival is associated with which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pola is a festival celebrated primarily in Maharashtra (particularly the Vidarbha region) and parts of Chhattisgarh, dedicated to honouring bulls and oxen for their role in agriculture. (पोला त्यौहार — महाराष्ट्र)

 

• The festival is observed on the Amavasya (new moon day) of the Shravan month, marking the end of the sowing season, and involves decorating and worshipping bullocks, followed by processions.

 

• Pola highlights the deep agrarian connection between farmers and their draught animals in rural Maharashtra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of Maharashtra include Gudi Padwa (New Year) and Ganesh Chaturthi.

 

• A similar bull-worship tradition, Pongal's Mattu Pongal, is observed in Tamil Nadu.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagaland (Option 1): Known for festivals such as the Hornbill Festival, not Pola.

 

• Mizoram (Option 2): Known for festivals such as Chapchar Kut, not Pola.

 

• Karnataka (Option 4): Not associated with the Pola festival.

question: Which of the following facts cannot be attributed as a reason for microfinance?
option_1: Financial services can enable the poor to benefit from their entrepreneurial efforts
option_2: Financial services can enable the poor to speed up the process of building economic security and reducing insecurity
option_3: Financial services can enable the poor to earn high interest rates on their deposits
option_4: Financial services can enable the poor to speed up income-generating activities
solution_text:
The correct answer is Financial services can enable the poor to earn high interest rates on their deposits.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Microfinance refers to small-scale financial services (small loans, savings, insurance) provided to poor and low-income individuals who lack access to conventional banking. (सूक्ष्म वित्त — गरीबों तक पहुँच)

 

• The core rationale for microfinance is to help the poor access credit for entrepreneurial/income-generating activity, build economic security, and reduce vulnerability — not to offer them unusually high interest on deposits.

 

• In fact, microfinance institutions typically charge relatively higher interest on the small loans they extend (to cover their higher administrative cost per loan), rather than offering high returns on deposits.

 

• The stated purpose of microfinance is thus centred on access to credit and savings facilities, not on generating high deposit returns for the poor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In India, microfinance is largely delivered through the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (SBLP) and Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) regulated by the RBI.

 

• NABARD has played a pioneering role in promoting Self-Help Groups (SHGs) as a channel for microfinance in rural India.

 

NOTE

 

• Benefiting from entrepreneurial efforts (Option 1): A genuine, standard justification for microfinance.

 

• Speeding up economic security / reducing insecurity (Option 2): A genuine, standard justification for microfinance.

 

• Speeding up income-generating activities (Option 4): A genuine, standard justification for microfinance.

question: In which year was the first railway line in India built?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1853.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first passenger railway line was inaugurated on 16 April 1853, running between Bori Bunder (Bombay) and Thane, a distance of about 34 km. (भारत की पहली रेलवे लाइन — 1853)

 

• The train was operated by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR) and was hauled by three steam locomotives named Sahib, Sindh and Sultan.

 

• This event marked the formal beginning of the railway network in India, which would go on to become one of the largest rail networks in the world.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first goods train ran even earlier, in 1851, in Roorkee for construction purposes.

 

• The 16th of April is commemorated in Indian railway history as the day of the first official passenger train run.

 

NOTE

 

• 1887 (Option 1): Not the year of India's first railway line.

 

• 1888 (Option 2): Not the year of India's first railway line.

 

• 1890 (Option 4): Not the year of India's first railway line.

question: In 1662, who described that when a gas is enclosed in a closed vessel/container, it compresses to fit the space, but the pressure exerted by the gas on the container increases?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Robert Boyle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This description corresponds to Boyle's Law, formulated by the Irish scientist Robert Boyle in 1662. (बॉयल का नियम — रॉबर्ट बॉयल, 1662)

 

• Boyle's Law states that, at constant temperature, the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its volume (P ∝ 1/V, or PV = constant).

 

• This means if a gas is compressed into a smaller container, its volume decreases while the pressure it exerts increases proportionally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Charles's Law (by Jacques Charles) relates the volume of a gas to its temperature at constant pressure (V ∝ T).

 

• Gay-Lussac's Law relates pressure to temperature at constant volume, and Avogadro's Law relates volume to the number of moles of gas at constant temperature and pressure.

 

NOTE

 

• Joseph Gay Lussac (Option 1): Associated with the pressure-temperature law (Gay-Lussac's Law), not this 1662 pressure-volume relationship.

 

• Jacques Charles (Option 3): Associated with the volume-temperature law (Charles's Law), not this 1662 relationship.

 

• Amedeo Avogadro (Option 4): Associated with Avogadro's Law (volume-mole number relationship) and Avogadro's number, not this 1662 relationship.

question: Which Indian state is known as 'Kuhl', a traditional canal irrigation system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Kuhl' is a traditional surface canal irrigation system practised in the hill state of Himachal Pradesh, particularly in the Kangra region. (कुहल सिंचाई प्रणाली — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

 

• A Kuhl channels water from a natural stream or glacier-fed source through a temporary/permanent diversion structure into a network of gravity-flow channels that irrigate terraced fields.

 

• These systems are traditionally built and managed by local communities through cooperative, customary arrangements (a 'Kohli' or water-manager oversees distribution).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similar traditional irrigation systems in other regions include Ahar-Pyne (Bihar/Jharkhand) and Zabo (Nagaland).

 

• Himachal Pradesh's Kuhl system exemplifies indigenous water management adapted to hilly, glacier-fed terrain.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 1): Not associated with the Kuhl irrigation system.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 2): Known for tank irrigation, not Kuhl.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Not associated with the Kuhl irrigation system.
